question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}y({x}^{2}+1),\, & -1\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $\text{E}[X]=0$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{2}{3},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$

If $\textrm{E}[X] = \dfrac{7}{12},$ $\textrm{E}[Y] = \dfrac{5}{8},$ and $\textrm{E}[XY]=\dfrac{17}{48},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274885/assets/41f5a511a7cd878ea6911d78ee12aa97941fb75b6d2ecd3f36084f9ded38ffcb.svg)

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm{E}[X^2] - \textrm{E}[X]^2,
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\textrm{Cov}[X,Y] = \textrm{E}[XY] - \textrm{E}[X] \cdot \textrm{E}[Y].
$$

First, we find $\textrm{Var}[X].$
We compute $\textrm{E}[X^2]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(x+\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}+\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}{y}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{4}y+\frac{1}{6}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}-{(\frac{7}{12})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{144}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\textrm{E}[Y^2]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}(x+\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x{y}^{2}+\frac{3}{2}{y}^{4})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{3}{2}x{y}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{3}{2}{y}^{4})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{6}{y}^{3}+\frac{3}{10}{y}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}+\frac{3}{10} \\  & =\frac{7}{15}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{15}-{(\frac{5}{8})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{73}{960}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's find $\textrm{Cov}[X,Y].$ Using the given results, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{17}{48}-(\frac{7}{12})\cdot (\frac{5}{8}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{96}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by
